meta.regime: The regime has changed character overnight. For three weeks it was an energy supply shock pushing the long end of the US curve around, with the Fed a passive passenger. As of 18:00Z yesterday the Fed is the driver again, and it is driving in one direction. The September projections did not merely confirm the hike to a 3.75%-4.00% range; they rebuilt the whole path, lifting the 2026 median to 4.1% from 3.8%, putting 16 of 18 participants behind at least one more increase this year, and doing it while revising growth UP to 2.3%, unemployment DOWN to 4.1% from 4.3% and core PCE UP to 3.4% from 3.3%. A stronger economy with firmer inflation and a lower unemployment path is the configuration that produces more hikes, and the committee said so in the only language it has. The second feature is that the energy leg is quietly deflating at the margin. WTI at 102.173 is now NEGATIVE on the week, Brent at 105.755 is -1.74%, and European gas has fallen 5.20% in Amsterdam and 6.08% in Britain over seven days - the first sustained relief since the Petroline strikes. That does not end the shock, because the monthly numbers are still +21.55% on WTI and +22.20% on EU gas and refined products remain the tight leg with heating oil +17.30% on the month, but it does change which currencies are helped and hurt at the margin: it takes the floor out from under CAD and puts one under EUR. The third feature is a caution against simply buying the dollar with both hands. The move has largely happened - DXY is +1.23% on the week - Warsh explicitly said the Fed does not at this stage envisage an aggressive tightening cycle, and TE's own model still carries 4.00% at the October 28 meeting, which is a hold. Two central banks report inside the next sixteen hours. The correct posture is to hold the dollar longs that already worked and to express the rest of the board through crosses.

update.title: 🇯🇵 JPY analysis updated
update.text: BoJ hiked to 1.25% from 1.00%, exactly in line. The yen FELL on it - USD/JPY 156.586, +0.39%. JPY holds +1; Ueda at 06:30Z is now the entire event.

meta.nextBigEvent: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda's press conference, today September 18 at 06:30Z - three and a half hours after a statement that has already been released and already been spent. The hike itself carried no information: TE's actual printed 1.25% against a 1.25% consensus and TE's own house forecast, previous 1.00%, which is as fully priced as a central-bank decision gets. What the tape then did is the reason this is still the biggest event on the board. The yen did not rally on 25bp of delivered tightening - it fell, with USD/JPY 156.586 and +0.39% on the session, +1.93% on the week and a sixth consecutive session of underperformance. Underneath that sits the print from 23:30Z last night that the market has barely discussed: August national core CPI eased to 1.7% from 1.8%, BELOW the 1.8% consensus, so the inflation series the board would need to justify a continued path toward 1.50% softened in the twelve hours before it hiked. Ueda therefore arrives with one genuinely difficult sentence to write. Confirming that normalisation continues, and linking yen weakness to imported inflation, is the route that restores JPY to +2 and breaks every XXX/JPY cross lower from a crowded position. A data-dependent framing with no terminal-rate steer - the configuration Reuters reported ahead of the meeting - cuts JPY to zero and makes USD/JPY a clean long into whatever level the Ministry of Finance chooses to defend, and at 156.59 that is the second live variable, because the MoF bought yen eleven days ago at a better level and the Takaichi administration is openly opposed to further depreciation. Do not carry size through 06:30Z in either direction. The next scheduled event after it is a six-week vacuum to the October 30 meeting, where TE's model carries an unchanged 1.25% alongside the Quarterly Outlook Report.

dailyRead: Start with the correction this file owes, because it is the most useful thing on the page. For two sessions the argument here was that the June dot plot had become a DOVISH landmine: futures priced two more 2026 hikes against a June median of one, so confirming June would read dovish and hit the dollar longs. The September projections landed at 18:00Z and did the opposite. The 2026 median moved UP to 4.1% from 3.8%, which carries one further hike from the new 3.75%-4.00% range; TE's series shows the out-year median lifted to 3.9% from 3.4% and press accounts put 2027 nearer 4.1% from 3.6%, so on either reading the easing path that defined the June dots is gone. Sixteen of eighteen participants project at least one more increase across the final two meetings of 2026. And the supporting forecasts moved the same way rather than offsetting: real GDP to 2.3% from 2.2%, unemployment to 4.1% from 4.3% across 2026-2028, PCE to 3.7% and core PCE to 3.4% from 3.3%. Warsh then removed the ambiguity in the press conference - this summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved - and said the standard for a pause had not been satisfied. USD goes to +3 because the +3 trigger written on this page yesterday morning required confirmed projections carrying a further 2026 hike with flattened out-years, and what arrived was better than that: the out-years rose. The market agreed without hesitation. DXY is 100.265 with the week +1.23% and the month +0.61%, against a month that was NEGATIVE at -0.05% twenty-four hours before the release - the single figure this file kept flagging as the warning underneath every dollar long, now resolved. EUR/USD 1.14669 and -1.25% on the week, GBP/USD 1.33812 and -0.97%, USD/CHF 0.82552 and +1.56%, USD/CAD 1.39882 and +1.12%, NZD/USD 0.57279 and -1.19%, and USD/JPY through 155 to 156.005 with the week +1.02%. It is also worth recording that yesterday's US retail sales beat properly and in the right place: 1.2% m/m against a 0.9% consensus after -0.5%, with the CONTROL GROUP at 1.4% against 0.4% expected and ex-autos 1.4% - not a fuel-price illusion, which is what this file said to check for. The second board change is CAD, cut from +1 to 0, and the reason is that a leg broke rather than that a risk appeared. The Canadian +1 has rested for two weeks on terms of trade: a frozen central bank at 2.25% offset by an oil windfall. As of this morning the windfall has stopped. WTI's WEEKLY figure is NEGATIVE at -0.30%, against +8.95% at the same point last week, Brent is -1.74% on the week, and the Petroline restart that prediction markets price at 84.5% by September 30 has not even landed yet. Underneath that, the domestic picture got worse in a way that had nothing to do with oil: services PMI fell to 46.8 from 49.1, a deepening contraction in the larger part of the economy, on top of August employment at -41,700, retail sales at -0.8% and a monthly CPI of -0.1% that keeps the Bank of Canada pinned. A currency whose only argument was energy, in a week when energy stopped paying, is a zero. The consequences are mechanical and worth stating plainly: EUR/CAD and GBP/CAD leave SHORT, CAD/CHF leaves LONG, AUD/CAD becomes a mild LONG and USD/CAD improves. Third, a tailwind that arrived without a headline: European gas is finally falling. EU gas is 77.78 and -5.20% on the WEEK, UK gas 192.60 and -6.08%, German gas 78.95 and -2.48% on the day alone. Those monthly figures are still brutal at +22.20% and +26.66%, and storage near 68% of capacity is below the five-year average, so this is relief rather than repair - but it is the first sustained fall in a month and it lands on the euro's single biggest weakness. It is why EUR holds +1 despite a genuinely soft Q2 wage print of 3.0% against 3.4% previously, which is the ECB's own second-round-effects gauge cooling six days after a hawkish hike, and why GER40 comes off SHORT to RANGE. Fourth, the metals deserve credit for what they did NOT do. The bear case for gold and silver has always been rising US real yields; yesterday delivered the most hawkish Fed event of the cycle with the 10-year around 5%, and gold fell only to roughly 4264 before bouncing to 4298.04, +0.80%, with silver +0.79% at 63.740. A market that gets its bearish catalyst and refuses to break is not a market to re-short, which is why both stay RANGE rather than going back to SHORT - but the weekly at -0.45% and the hawkish path equally rule out a long. Finally, two decisions inside sixteen hours. The Bank of England at 11:00Z is a priced hold where only the vote split matters, and the distribution is one-sided: a 3-0-6 repeat does nothing while any defection from the three hike votes cuts GBP to -1. The Bank of Japan at 02:30Z tomorrow hikes to 1.25% with near-certainty, which is precisely why the terminal-rate language is the event - and USD/JPY at 156.005 is now in the zone where the Ministry of Finance bought yen ten days ago. JPY holds +1 on tomorrow's hike and that intervention risk, not on price action, because the price action has been one-way against it for five sessions. The cleanest expressions today are the dollar longs that already have the wind - NZD/USD and USD/CHF - and the dollar-free kiwi shorts, EUR/NZD and AUD/NZD. Nothing is HIGH conviction into two central banks.

today.read: The tail this page flagged since Tuesday was one-sided and dated: any erosion of the three hike votes, or minutes leaning on the labour-market deterioration, cuts GBP to -1. Forward: the score stays at ZERO because an in-line hold with an in-line vote is not new tightening and the hawkish route stayed shut when core CPI held at 2.6% on Tuesday - but the uncertainty discount that capped every GBP ticket comes off, so conviction improves on GBP/USD and GBP/AUD without any bias flipping. Both figures landed exactly in line, so the priced outcome is the outcome and sterling barely moved: GBP/USD 1.33798, -0.01% on the day. The path itself is unchanged - hold - but the reasons behind it are now confirmed rather than forecast. Three members again preferred 4.00%, a fourth consecutive meeting of hawkish dissent, and nobody voted to cut. That matters more than the repeat itself, because the labour market gave the doves everything they needed since July: claimant count +27.8K against an 8.3K forecast, payrolled employees -26.1K in August, wage growth down to 3.9% from 4.2%, retail sales -0.5% m/m. A committee handed that data and still returning a 0/9 cut row is a committee with no dovish wing, which puts a firmer near-term floor under the pound than the data alone suggests. The rest of the TE-verified picture is unchanged: CPI 3.1% y/y with core HELD at 2.6% for a fourth month and services 3.4%, unemployment 4.9%, GDP +0.4% q/q and 1.2% annual, manufacturing PMI 51.7, services 52.5, consumer confidence -14, business confidence -36 from -65. What now sits between this decision and the next: retail sales tomorrow at 06:00Z, expected -0.2% m/m, then a six-week vacuum in which no scheduled repricing is available. The hawkish route to a November hike needs services inflation back above 3.4%; the dovish route needs the labour market to crack far enough to create a cut vote where there is currently none.

strength.tag: Hawkish dots: 2026 median 4.1%, 16 of 18 want more
strength.drivers: Fed funds upper bound 4.00% after the first hike since 2023; the September projections lifted the 2026 median to 4.1% from 3.8% with 16 of 18 participants behind at least one more increase, and revised real GDP up to 2.3%, unemployment DOWN to 4.1% from 4.3% and core PCE up to 3.4%; CPI 3.4% with core 2.4%, payrolls +162,000, retail sales +1.2% m/m with the control group +1.4% against 0.4% expected; DXY 100.265, week +1.23%, month +0.61%.
strength.forward: 🦅 Tightening, and upgraded from +2 to +3 on a trigger this file wrote down in advance. The trigger required confirmed projections carrying a further 2026 hike with flattened out-years. What landed was stronger: the out-years rose as well. TE's calendar carries both projection rows - 1st Yr 4.1% against 3.6% previously, 2nd Yr 3.9% against 3.4% - and press accounts of the same release put the 2026 median at 4.1% from 3.8% and 2027 nearer 4.1% from 3.6%. The labels differ between series; the substance does not. The median now carries one more hike this year and the June easing path is gone. Sixteen of eighteen participants project at least one further increase across October and December. Critically, the supporting forecasts did not offset it: growth was revised UP to 2.3%, the unemployment path DOWN to 4.1% across 2026-2028 from 4.3%, and core PCE UP to 3.4%. Stronger growth with lower unemployment and firmer inflation is the exact configuration that produces more tightening, and Warsh said so plainly - this summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved, and the standard for a pause has not been satisfied. This file spent two sessions arguing the opposite case and it was wrong; recording that is more useful than defending it. Yesterday's retail sales deserve a line too, because this page said to check the control group rather than the headline for a fuel-price illusion: the control group printed +1.4% against 0.4% expected and ex-autos +1.4%, so the beat was real. Now the discipline. The move has largely happened - DXY +1.23% on the week - Warsh explicitly said the Fed does not at this stage envisage an aggressive tightening cycle, and TE's own model carries 4.00% at October 28, which is a hold. So +3 means hold the dollar longs that already worked and express the rest of the board through crosses, not add into a made move ahead of two other central banks. What takes USD off +3: a soft Philly Fed at 12:30Z today, forecast 31.3 after 47.4, with claims above 207K - the first crack in the growth leg these projections just leaned on. Consumer confidence has already dropped to 47.8 from 51.7.

strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced, and held at +1 because the day produced one fact against the euro and one for it at roughly equal weight. Against: Q2 wage growth at 3.0%, down from 3.4%, with negotiated wage growth 2.44% from 2.56%. That is the ECB's own preferred second-round-effects gauge, and it cooled six days after a package that raised the deposit rate to 2.50%, revised 2027 inflation up to 2.5% and 2028 to 2.1%, upgraded growth, named the Middle East conflict as continuing to fuel inflationary pressures, and had Lagarde place inflation risks to the UPSIDE. A hawkish central bank whose wage evidence is softening underneath it has a credibility problem, and that is the specific route to EUR zero - it would mean the September package was the peak rather than the start. For the euro, and genuinely new: the energy drag is easing. EU gas is 77.78 and -5.20% on the WEEK, UK gas 192.60 and -6.08%, German gas 78.95 and -2.48% on the day alone. Keep it in proportion, because this file has been wrong before by over-reading a single energy session: the monthly figures are still +22.20% and +26.66%, EU storage near 68% of capacity is below the five-year average, and the structural bid from Asian competition for Atlantic LNG cargoes is intact. But the weekly direction has changed for the first time in a month, and it lands on precisely the thing that has capped every euro rally since August - a terms-of-trade drag that was intensifying and is now easing. Those two offset, so the score holds. The cleaner observation is relative: EUR/USD at 1.14669 is +0.02% on the day and -1.25% on the week, which means the euro is not falling on its own account, it is being carried down by a dollar that just got hawkish projections. That is why the euro is still the best funding-side long against the kiwi and the best home for a Canada-neutral view. Final August HICP at 09:00Z today should confirm 3.3% and core 2.4%. Lagarde speaks tomorrow at 10:30Z and is the next thing that can move it. What takes EUR to zero: Lagarde acknowledging the wage slowdown.

strength.tag: Hiked to 1.25% in line - and the yen fell on it
strength.drivers: BoJ policy rate RAISED to 1.25% from 1.00% at 03:00Z, actual matching both the 1.25% consensus and TE's 1.25% house forecast; wage growth 4.7% - the strongest in the G10 - unemployment 2.4% and falling, GDP +0.4% q/q, manufacturing PMI 54.9, retail sales +2.4% m/m; against that, August core CPI eased to 1.7% from 1.8% and BELOW the 1.8% forecast, the trade balance widened to -1,106bn yen from -638bn, and USD/JPY is 156.586 and +0.39% on the day with the week +1.93%.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced, HELD AT +1, and the reason it is held rather than cut is a written rule rather than a preference. This page has carried one dated downgrade trigger for the yen all week - an explicit pause signal - and no such signal is in hand, because the statement is out and the press conference is not. Cutting the score three and a half hours before the only part of the meeting that contains information would be trading the clock rather than the evidence. What must be said plainly is that the case underneath the +1 is now materially thinner than it was yesterday. Yesterday the +1 was explicitly carried by a hike that had not yet landed. It has now landed, exactly as priced - TE-verified at 1.25% actual against a 1.25% consensus and a 1.25% TE house forecast, up from 1.00%, the second increase in four months - and the currency went the other way. USD/JPY is 156.586, +0.39% on the session and +1.93% on the week, a sixth consecutive session of yen underperformance and the first to come with 25bp of real tightening behind it. A currency that cannot rally on its own catalyst has told you something, and the something is that the entire move was pre-positioned between 160 and 153 over the preceding weeks and is now unwinding. Then the fact that deserves more attention than it is getting: at 23:30Z last night, twelve hours before the board voted, August national core CPI came in at 1.7% against a 1.8% consensus and DOWN from 1.8%, with headline unchanged at 1.9%. The inflation series the BoJ would have to point at to keep 1.50% credibly in view decelerated and undershot on the eve of the decision. That is a genuine dovish counterweight to a hawkish action, and it cuts directly against the sell-side view - a Reuters poll on September 10 carried 1.75% by Q2 2027 - while sitting closer to TE's own econometric model, which reads October 30 as an unchanged 1.25% and then trends the rate back toward 1.00% in 2027. The two supports that survive are concrete. First, 1.25% is real tightening in a world where the Fed is the only other central bank moving, and the domestic case remains intact on wages at 4.7%, the highest in the G10, and unemployment at 2.4% and falling. Second, 156.59 is deeper into the zone where the Ministry of Finance bought yen eleven days ago at a better level, with the Takaichi administration openly opposed to further depreciation - and the probability of a violent reversal is a function of the level, which has got worse again. The structural drag is unchanged: the trade balance at -1,106bn yen from -638bn is the Gulf energy bill arriving in Japan's external accounts, and no 25bp hike offsets it. One process note, because it matters for how this is read: the vote split has not been published in any source reachable from here and is NOT assumed. Takata dissented for exactly this 1.25% at the July meeting, when the hold carried 8-1. Practically, every yen cross stays at RANGE or LOW conviction and nothing is sized through the press conference. What restores +2: Ueda keeping the path toward 1.50% explicitly open, or naming yen weakness as an imported-inflation risk. What cuts to zero: a data-dependent framing with no terminal-rate steer, which makes USD/JPY a clean long into whatever level the MoF defends. Both are resolved at 06:30Z today.

strength.tag: BoE held 3.75% on a 3-0-6 vote - both tails failed to fire
strength.drivers: BoE HELD Bank Rate at 3.75% on a 3-0-6 vote, TE-verified with the MPC Vote Hike row actual at 3/9 and the MPC Vote Cut row actual at 0/9, both exactly in line; CPI 3.1% y/y with core HELD at 2.6% for a fourth month and services 3.4%; against a claimant count of +27.8K versus 8.3K expected, payrolled employees -26.1K, wage growth 3.9% from 4.2%, unemployment 4.9%, retail sales -0.5% m/m; GBP/USD 1.33798, day -0.01%, week -0.98%.
strength.forward: ⚖️ Balanced, HELD AT ZERO through the decision, and the score does not move because nothing in the release justified moving it - but the character of the zero has changed completely and that is the tradeable content. This page carried an explicit, dated downgrade trigger since Tuesday: any erosion of the three hike votes to 2 or 1, or minutes leaning on the labour-market deterioration, cuts GBP to -1 and takes GBP/USD, GBP/NZD and EUR/GBP with it. It did not fire. TE's MPC Vote Hike row printed 3/9 against a 3/9 consensus and the Vote Cut row printed 0/9, so the split repeated July exactly: three for 4.00%, none for a cut, six unchanged. Read what that actually required. Since the July meeting the UK labour market has deteriorated on every series the doves would use - the claimant count jumped 27.8K against an 8.3K forecast on Monday, payrolled employees fell 26.1K in August, wage growth decelerated to 3.9% from 4.2%, retail sales are -0.5% m/m - and against all of it not one member moved to the dovish side and not one of the three hawks stood down. The non-obvious point is the empty half of the committee: with the cut row at 0/9, there is currently no dovish wing at all on this MPC, so the near-term policy floor is firmer than the labour data alone would imply. That is the first meeting since April at which the hawkish minority neither grew nor shrank - 8-1, 7-2, 6-3, 6-3 - which reads as a committee that has settled rather than one drifting toward a cut. Why this is still zero and not +1: an in-line hold with an in-line vote is not new tightening, the hawkish route remains closed because core CPI and services did not move on Tuesday, and the price agrees - GBP/USD is 1.33798 and -0.01% on the day, a fully priced event doing exactly nothing. What changes practically is the risk premium rather than the score: the single largest scheduled sterling event of the month has passed without damage, so the uncertainty discount that capped conviction on every GBP ticket comes off, and the pound reverts to a relative-score story against a USD at +3 and an AUD at +1. Next inputs: retail sales tomorrow at 06:00Z, expected -0.2% m/m after -0.5%, then a six-week policy vacuum to November 5 at 12:00Z. What cuts GBP to -1 now: a second consecutive negative retail sales print alongside another labour-market miss, which would put a cut back on a committee that currently has nobody arguing for one. What takes it to +1: services inflation re-accelerating above 3.4% in the September CPI, which is the only route left for the three hawks to gain a fourth vote.

catalysts.note: RELEASED, and it resolved against this file's own two-day warning. The rate was roughly 92% priced and carried no information; the projections were always the event, and they came in HAWKISH rather than the dovish landmine this page kept flagging. TE's calendar carries the projection rows at 4.1% against 3.6% previously and 3.9% against 3.4%; press accounts of the same release put the 2026 median at 4.1% from 3.8% in June and 2027 nearer 4.1% from 3.6%. The supporting forecasts reinforced it rather than offsetting: real GDP 2.3% from 2.2%, unemployment 4.1% from 4.3% held across 2026-2028, PCE 3.7% and core PCE 3.4% from 3.3%. USD moved from +2 to +3 on the trigger written here in advance.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC press conference (Warsh)
catalysts.note: RELEASED. Warsh removed the remaining ambiguity: this summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved, and the standard for a pause has not been satisfied. Set against that is the one genuine dovish qualifier of the day, and it is the reason the next meeting still reads as a hold rather than a hike - he also said the Fed does not at this stage envisage an aggressive tightening cycle, and TE's own model carries 4.00% at October 28. catalysts.note: The day's main event and the one asymmetric setup on the board. catalysts.note: RELEASED, TE-VERIFIED, and it resolved to the fully priced outcome. The second fact belongs beside it and is being under-read: at 23:30Z, twelve hours before the board voted, August national core CPI printed 1.7% against a 1.8% consensus and down from 1.8%, with headline unchanged at 1.9%. The board tightened on a morning when its own core inflation series was decelerating and undershooting, which makes hawkish continuation language harder to write than it looked yesterday. One caveat recorded rather than glossed: the vote split has not been published in any source reachable from here and is NOT assumed. Takata dissented for exactly this 1.25% in July, when the hold carried 8-1. JPY holds +1 - the written downgrade trigger was an explicit pause signal and no such signal is in hand - but the score is now a hold into the press conference rather than a conviction call, resting on the delivered rate and on intervention risk at 156.59 rather than on price action.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda press conference
catalysts.note: THE EVENT. 3:30pm Tokyo, three and a half hours after a statement that contained nothing the market had not already priced. Time corrected to 06:30Z - this file carried 05:30Z yesterday and that was wrong. With the hike delivered at 1.25%, TE-verified in line with consensus and TE's own forecast, the entire tradeable content of the meeting is how Ueda frames what comes next: pausing to assess, or continuing toward 1.50%. He arrives with a harder sentence to write than he expected. The domestic case for continuing is available - wage growth 4.7%, the strongest in the G10, unemployment 2.4% and falling, services PMI 52.5 - but August core CPI eased to 1.7% from 1.8% and BELOW the 1.8% consensus at 23:30Z last night, so the inflation series he would point at has just softened. The constraint pushing the other way is the currency: at 156.586, after the yen FELL on its own hike, a dovish framing risks an immediate test of the intervention zone the Ministry of Finance defended eleven days ago, which gives the Bank an unusual incentive to sound hawkier than the sourced pre-meeting reports suggested. Two outcomes. Guidance keeping 1.50% explicitly open, or yen weakness named as an imported-inflation risk, restores JPY to +2 and breaks every yen cross lower from crowded positioning. A data-dependent framing with no terminal-rate steer cuts JPY to zero and makes USD/JPY a clean long into whatever level the MoF chooses to defend. Carry no size through it.

Vessel counts and claimed crude volumes are different measures and only the first is independently verifiable. What is not disputed is where the squeeze actually binds: refined products, with heating oil +17.30% and gasoline +6.08% on the month against crude's weekly turning negative. But the direction has changed for the first time since the Petroline strikes, and it lands on the euro's single biggest weakness. It is why EUR holds +1 through a soft wage print, why GER40 came off SHORT to RANGE, and why EUR/CAD left SHORT.

geopolitics: The honest starting point today is that this file over-corrected yesterday and the correction needs correcting. On Tuesday this page had been repeating that Strait of Hormuz traffic was running roughly 90% below pre-war levels; yesterday it withdrew that figure on the strength of US Energy Secretary Chris Wright putting crude transits above 17 million barrels per day against roughly 20 million before the February 28 attacks, and Treasury Secretary Bessent citing at least 10 million a day. That withdrawal was too confident, because the two numbers are not measuring the same thing and only one of them is independently verifiable. IMF PortWatch recorded 8 vessel transits on September 13 against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day, independent trackers now put the disruption past its 190th day, and Al Jazeera has reported traffic falling even as Washington insists the waterway is fully open. Vessel counts down roughly 90% and official claims of crude volumes down 15-25% can both be published, but they cannot both be describing the same waterway in the same way, and the official figure is contested rather than confirmed. The practical instruction is to stop treating either number as settled and to watch what is not in dispute. What is not in dispute is where the squeeze actually binds. Refined products remain the tight leg: heating oil is +17.30% on the month and gasoline +6.08%, and US pump diesel has been at record levels, while crude itself has gone flat with WTI at 102.173 and its WEEKLY figure NEGATIVE at -0.30% against +8.95% at this point last week, and Brent at 105.755 and -1.74%. That divergence is the single most useful thing on this page for positioning, because it tells you which headlines move the board: a refinery, products or shipping-insurance story reprices inflation and therefore rates; a crude-flow story increasingly does not. The second live thread is the Saudi East-West pipeline. Drones launched from Iraqi territory struck Petroline on September 10 and 11 while it was carrying roughly 5 million bpd of crude rerouted around Hormuz, putting about 4 million bpd at risk; Wright has said the interruption will be measured in days, prediction markets price an 84.5% chance of a restart by September 30, and Aramco demonstrated after the April strike that it can restore all 7 million bpd within days. Oil has stopped rising into that, which is the market pricing the restart before it happens. The FX read follows directly and produced today's second board change. Canada was cut from +1 to 0 because the terms-of-trade leg that carried it went flat BEFORE its known negative catalyst landed, which is the worst sequencing a commodity-currency trade can have; a currency whose only argument is energy, in a week when energy stopped paying, is a neutral. In the opposite direction, Europe finally caught a break: EU gas is -5.20% on the week, UK gas -6.08% and German gas -2.48% on the day, the first sustained fall since the strikes, which is why EUR holds +1 through a soft wage print and why GER40 came off SHORT. The franc keeps its haven floor - the SNB named Middle East tensions in June as a risk that could STRENGTHEN the franc alongside a signalled readiness to intervene - which is why CHF is held at zero rather than cut despite the widest policy gap on the board. And Japan now carries the energy shock in its external accounts directly, with the trade balance widening to -1,106bn yen from -638bn, a structural drag that this morning's 25bp hike to 1.25% plainly does not offset - the yen fell on the decision, USD/JPY 156.586 and +0.39%. The standing risk to every one of these positions is the same: this is an active war, the restart is a headline rather than a fact, and a second strike on Petroline or a products-infrastructure hit reverses the oil leg, the gas relief, the Canadian cut and the euro's reprieve in a single session.
